results.fact: Where the summit day leaves the trail
results.evidence: The published route description (quoting the Olympic climbers' guide) says the Marmot Lake route leaves the trail three miles above Duckabush Camp and follows a little creek into an amphitheater on the west side of the summit. The trail-crew report puts Marmot Lake 3.3 mi above Upper Duckabush Camp (2.2 mi to the ford + 1.1 mi), so the turnoff is at or just below Marmot Lake - supporting beta, the itinerary and the approach text, and contradicting waypoints[2]/[5] and approach_variants[0] ('about 3 mi below Marmot Lake'). Not patched: only one route source states the turnoff, and waypoints[2]'s own coordinate sits east of the summit at ~2,830 ft ground elevation (near Upper Duckabush Camp), so rewriting its note would leave the pin contradicting it; pin positions are out of scope.

results.evidence: The only route description found says that from First Divide you go west into a basin with a nameless lake, then descend southwest toward the saddle between the two peaks of Mt Steel and follow the ridge north to the summit block - agreeing with approach, climbing_route[1] and approach_variants[1], against beta's Duckabush-Steel saddle. Other pages found are copies of that text; no second independent source, and the internal majority (3 fields, no waypoints) is below the internal-plus-one threshold.

The parking line says no park entrance fee is charged to PARK at the Forest Service trailhead (a Northwest Forest Pass applies there); the other fields say an entrance pass applies on crossing into the park. The park's fee page says every visitor needs an entrance pass, with a $15 per-person rate for those entering on foot, and a trail guide for this basin lists a federal park pass for park entry - so both statements hold.

results.evidence: The park's wilderness-reservations page says permits in non-quota areas are not limited and can be reserved online or picked up at a permit office, while no sites are held as same-day walk-ups. The Steel route page says the wilderness permit can be obtained at ranger stations, and a permit guide says permits are issued in person at park visitor centers. So access.permit is right; overnight_permit.where's flat 'no same-day walk-up permits' overstated it and its Flapjack Lakes canister clause belongs to a different drainage. The Staircase closure note is kept because it governs the First Divide approach.

results.evidence: A detailed first-hand report from Royal Basin describes camping in the lower basin, bushwhacking west through a ~700-ft brushy forest band to a talus tongue below the complex E face, climbing NW to the south end of Gray Wolf Ridge, passing 4-5 pinnacles by class 3 moves on their east side, then the NE ridge and a sharp blade to the summit - matching beta's brush crux and the itinerary's north-ridge blade. The peak's reference page lists the easiest route as class 3 via the West Side or Gray Wolf Ridge. A guidebook-derived description for a Royal/Deception Basin line instead climbs a west gully to the east ridge 150 yd SE of the summit, which resembles the row's approach text. So at least two real lines exist and the row blends them (plus a Baldy-side pitch_detail that bypasses the summit). Settling this needs a rewrite of approach, pitch_detail and waypoints, not a minimal patch.

The park's Royal Basin page gives the climb as 2,550 ft to 5,100 ft over 7.2 miles. A climbing-club Royal Basin page puts the parking area just past the Dungeness River bridge at 2,500 ft. USGS 3DEP ground elevation at the row's trailhead pin is 2,494 ft. The row's itinerary already uses 2,550 ft of gain to the 5,100-ft lake, so 2,550 makes every field agree.
